public_rationale: In a post on 5 August 2024, Ed Zitron wrote that 'we're not quite at the bubble popping yet.' In the same passage he named OpenAI's collapse as 'the event'. He said it would mean Microsoft had cut OpenAI off and there was not enough banker or venture capital interest to prop it up. A report published on 29 August 2024, citing the WSJ, said Thrive Capital would lead a funding round with a commitment of about $1 billion and that Microsoft was expected to contribute (e1). A report the same day, citing Bloomberg, said OpenAI was closing in on a deal that would value it at more than $100 billion (e2). These reports describe investors, including Microsoft, expected to fund OpenAI in August 2024, not a cut-off. On 5 August 2024 TechCrunch reported that co-founder John Schulman had left for Anthropic and that OpenAI confirmed Greg Brockman was taking an extended leave (e3). That report does not mention a cut-off by Microsoft or other funders. Only his statement that the popping had not yet happened is assessed. His suggestion that it was close is not.
limitations: The funding reports were published on 29 August 2024, after the 5 August post. They describe reported talks and expected contributions, not a completed round.

Both funding reports come from outlets citing other publications: the WSJ (e1) and Bloomberg (e2). The Bloomberg original returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. The WSJ original was not among the sources considered.
e3 covers only staff departures and a leave confirmed on 5 August 2024. It does not describe OpenAI's wider operations or finances.
The evidence does not test how close OpenAI was to the collapse he described, which 'not quite' implies. That is a judgement and is not assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of August 2024, the generative AI bubble has not yet popped.

statement.excerpt: To be clear, we’re not quite at the bubble popping yet.

from_speaker: "we're not quite at the bubble popping yet"
"The reason I choose the collapse of OpenAI as 'the event'"
collapse would mean Microsoft cut it off and there wasn't enough banker or venture capital interest to prop it up
our_interpretation: In the same passage the speaker defines the popping as the collapse of OpenAI, meaning Microsoft cuts it off and bankers and venture capital will not prop it up. Plain reading: as of the post (early August 2024), OpenAI had not collapsed and investors were still willing to fund it.
The target period is August 2024, the month of the post. The claim describes the state at the time of writing.
'Not quite' suggests the popping was close. That nearness is a judgement and is not tested. Only 'not yet popped' is tested.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from August 2024 shows OpenAI operating and still attracting investment, with no sign that Microsoft or other funders had cut it off.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence shows that by early August 2024 OpenAI had collapsed, or had been cut off by Microsoft and investors, or that AI funding had already broadly dried up.
